gerados.Text: A healthy, well-fed adult sits at {{c1::zero}} nitrogen balance — neither positive nor negative.
gerados.Extra: Balance = N ingested − N excreted (~90% as urinary urea). Positive = net retention (growth, pregnancy, healing); negative = net loss (fasting, trauma, infection). Positive isn’t “good” nor negative “bad” — they only describe the direction of nitrogen flux.

gerados.Text: Deamination releases nitrogen as free ammonia: {{c1::glutamate dehydrogenase}} strips the amino group from glutamate, regenerating α-ketoglutarate.
gerados.Extra: This is the step that actually REMOVES nitrogen from the carbon skeleton — transamination had only transferred it onto glutamate. Mitochondrial, hepatic; uses NAD⁺/NADP⁺. It is what separates “transfer” from “eliminate”.
